newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Akzo Nobel Q1 up, repeats higher 97 ahead.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Akzo Nobel Q1 up, repeats higher 97 ahead.

text.p: Dutch chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Friday first-quarter profits edged up 2.4 percent to 340 million guilders ($176.3 million) and reiterated its forecast of higher earnings over the full year.
The profit rise was supported by better results at all divisions except fibres and improved exchange rates, Akzo said.
"Pharma, Coating and Chemicals did better than last year, while Fibers reported lower earnings," it said in a statement.
"(Akzo Nobel) maintains the expectation expressed earlier of higher profits in 1997 than in 1996," it said.
Akzo said at the presentation of annual results in February it expected net profits in 1997 to exceed the record 1.32 billion guilders of 1996.
First quarter operating income at Akzo's fibres unit more than halved to 18 million guilders from a year-earlier 45 million, undermined by strong price pressure.
Akzo Nobel added that generally higher currency exchange rates had also boosted earnings. The company's pharmaceuticals activities in particular have significant dollar exposure.
The group's high-margin pharmaceuticals and coatings divisions posted operating income up 15 million guilders to 198 million and 27 million to 108 million guilders respectively.
Its chemicals division, focus of recent restructuring and also dollar-sensitive, posted operating profits up 20 million guilders to 204 million.
However, group net profits came in at the lower end of analysts' forecasts of 332-380 million guilders and gained only a lukewarm welcome.

"(My) first reaction is that (the figures) are a little disappointing and primarily in the two so-called high quality units, coatings and pharmaceuticals," commented Tony Cox of London brokers Kleinwort Benson.
He said coatings had performed "considerably worse" than expected while profit growth at pharmaceuticals had slowed quarter on quarter.
But MeesPierson's Peter Schouten was much more upbeat, encouraged by the performance in chemicals.
"To me, chemicals are the main eye-catcher, far better than expected, outstanding," he said. "Probably the effects of the costly restructurings are trickling through."
Akzo shares, which had been trading some 1.0-1.50 guilders lower ahead of the figures, fell further on the results to stand 11.30 guilders down at 260.40 at 1410 GMT in a depressed Amsterdam market.
